notes: Hand-entered values. Masses in solar masses, distances in parsecs, ICRS RA/Dec in degrees. Disk parameters (tMaxK, lum, rOut, riaf*, mesh*) are display choices, not measurements (Cyg X-1 tMaxK 8e6 K matches the ~0.5-1 keV inner-disk temperatures of its soft state; colours clamp at 40000 K); incDeg/paDeg orient the disk axis on the sky (i > 90 = clockwise).

holes.name: Sgr A*
holes.description: The 4 million solar-mass black hole at the centre of the Milky Way; the Event Horizon Telescope imaged its shadow in 2022. In visible light it is a faint, radiatively inefficient flow ('Realistic'); 'Illustrative' shows a bright thin disk instead.
holes.source: Mass 4.30e6 Msun (project catalogue value; GRAVITY Collaboration 2019 A&A 625 L10 gives 4.15e6, EHT 2022 ApJL 930 L12 4.0e6); position Reid & Brunthaler 2004 ApJ 616 872; disk orientation from GRAVITY 2018 A&A 618 L10 flare orbits (approximate)

holes.name: M87*
holes.description: The supermassive black hole in the giant elliptical galaxy M87, the first black-hole shadow ever imaged (Event Horizon Telescope, 2019). We see it nearly face-on, 17 degrees from its jet axis.
holes.source: EHT Collaboration 2019 ApJL 875 L1, L5, L6 (mass, distance, 17 deg jet inclination, jet PA 288 deg); position NED

holes.name: Cygnus X-1

companion.name: HDE 226868
companion.source: Miller-Jones et al. 2021 Science 371 1046 (masses, inclination); radius and Teff Orosz et al. 2011 ApJ 742 84 (approximate); ephemeris Brocksopp et al. 1999 A&A 343 861 (approximate)

holes.description: The first black hole ever identified (1971): a 21 solar-mass hole feeding on the wind of the blue supergiant HDE 226868 in a 5.6-day orbit. The accretion stream drawn here is illustrative.
holes.source: Miller-Jones et al. 2021 Science 371 1046 (mass, 2.22 kpc parallax distance); position SIMBAD

holes.name: Gaia BH1
holes.description: The nearest known black hole: a dormant 9.6 solar-mass hole orbited every 186 days by a Sun-like star, found with Gaia astrometry. It does not accrete, so only its lensing shows.

holes.name: Gaia BH2
holes.description: A dormant 8.9 solar-mass black hole with a red-giant companion on a 3.5-year orbit.

holes.name: Gaia BH3
holes.description: The most massive stellar black hole known in the Milky Way (33 solar masses). Dormant, with a metal-poor giant companion on an 11.6-year orbit.
holes.source: Gaia Collaboration, Panuzzo et al. 2024 A&A 686 L2

holes.name: V404 Cygni
holes.description: A low-mass X-ray binary that erupts every few decades (1938, 1989, 2015) when its disk dumps matter onto the 9 solar-mass hole.
holes.source: Khargharia et al. 2010 ApJ 716 1105 (mass, inclination); Miller-Jones et al. 2009 ApJL 706 L230 (parallax distance)

holes.name: A0620-00
holes.description: One of the closest X-ray binaries: a 6.6 solar-mass black hole with a K-dwarf companion, quiet since its 1975 outburst.
